description: modules/crypto/native/ is excluded deliberately.
That Go module is OUT OF SCOPE for automation per spec
003-dependency-automation. The instruction is recorded in two places:
.github/workflows/scala-steward.yml ('the Go module under
modules/crypto/native/ is OUT OF SCOPE for automation') and
.scala-steward.conf ('gnark-crypto bumps remain manual until a future
spec replaces the Go path').
The bare onboarding config merged in #64 enabled the gomod manager
against the whole repo, and Renovate immediately opened #65 -- go 1.22
-> 1.26.8 plus gnark-crypto v0.13.0 -> v0.22.0 in exactly that
directory. That is the bump the spec reserves for a human, and it lands
on a native BN254 shim with its own build.sh and native-build workflow.
The root go.mod is left managed: it declares the module and a go
directive with no require block, so there is nothing there to get wrong.
JVM dependencies (build.mill, .mill-version) belong to Scala Steward --
see .scala-steward.conf. No guard is needed for them here because
Renovate has no Mill manager, so the two bots cannot collide on them.
CAP. The constitution pins JDK 21 LTS, and ./mill enforces it at runtime:
it exits 1 unless `java -version` reports 21 ('the constitution pins JDK
21 LTS'). Makefile sets MILL ?= ./mill and the `headers` target runs
SiidaBuild.millSiidaHeaderCheck, so a JDK bump fails at the first
Mill-using CI step rather than anywhere informative.
Renovate had grouped java-jdk 21 -> 25 and eclipse-temurin:21-jdk ->
25-jdk in with the action-version bumps, which is what reddened #79 at
'Check licence headers' (run 40000751608). Moving off 21 means changing
the constitution and the launcher guard together, so it is not a bump
Renovate should raise. The action versions in that group were fine and
landed separately.
Remove this rule when the constitution moves to a newer LTS.
